title: 11 — Document Intelligence and Financial NLP
html:
11 — Document Intelligence and Financial NLP

The one idea: much financial data arrives as PDFs — annual reports, factsheets, rating rationales. Document intelligence turns them into structured records in stages (layout → text and tables → entities → classification), and keeps, for every extracted number, the page and bounding box it came from. Without that provenance an extracted number cannot be checked, and an unchecked number cannot be published.

1. The staged pipeline

---
title: Document intelligence stages
---
flowchart LR
    PDF["Landed PDF<br/>(hash, manifest)"] --> PRE["Pre-flight:<br/>digital or scanned?<br/>redact personal data"]
    PRE --> LAY["Layout analysis<br/>(Docling / MinerU)"]
    LAY --> OCR["OCR for scanned pages<br/>(PaddleOCR / VLM)"]
    LAY --> TAB["Table structure"]
    OCR --> TAB
    TAB --> FLD["Field extraction<br/>+ GLiNER entities"]
    FLD --> CLS["Classification<br/>(FinBERT)"]
    CLS --> MAP["Map to ontology<br/>and identifiers"]
    MAP --> EVD["Evidence rows:<br/>page, bbox, confidence"]
    EVD --> GATE["Quality gate<br/>and human review"]
Stage Question it answers Tools
Pre-flight Text layer present? Encrypted? Personal data to mask? pypdf, heuristics
Layout Where are headings, paragraphs, tables, figures, reading order across columns? Docling, MinerU, LayoutLMv3
OCR What text is in this image region? PaddleOCR, dots.ocr, VLMs
Table structure Which cells form rows/columns, merged headers, totals? Docling TableFormer, Table Transformer, MinerU
Field extraction Which value is "Revenue from operations, FY26"? Rules + LLM/VLM + GLiNER
Classification Is this paragraph a going-concern doubt? Negative tone? FinBERT, fine-tuned classifiers
Mapping Which entity, which metric, which unit? Chapters 01 and 10

2. Digital vs scanned PDFs

Digital (born-digital) Scanned
Has an embedded text layer with exact character positions Pages are images; text must be recognised
Extract text directly — fast, exact OCR — slower, with errors (0 ↔ O, 1 ↔ l, missing decimal points)
Tables still need structure recognition Tables need OCR and structure

Check per page, not per file: many annual reports mix both (scanned signature pages, auditor's report as image).

3. Layout and table parsing with Docling

Docling converts PDFs (and DOCX, PPTX, HTML, images) into a structured document model with reading order, tables and provenance.

from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

conv = DocumentConverter()
result = conv.convert("landing/annual_report_fy26.pdf")
doc = result.document

markdown = doc.export_to_markdown()          # for reading, chunking for search
structured = doc.export_to_dict()            # full model, including provenance

for t_i, table in enumerate(doc.tables):
    df = table.export_to_dataframe()         # pandas DataFrame with header rows resolved
    prov = table.prov[0]                     # provenance: where on which page
    print(t_i, prov.page_no, prov.bbox)      # bbox has l, t, r, b and a coordinate origin

MinerU is an alternative strong on complex academic and financial layouts (multi-column, formulas, tables to HTML/Markdown). Evaluate both on your documents; the winner varies by publisher and template.

3.1 Bounding boxes and coordinate systems

A bounding box is [page, x0, y0, x1, y1]. Two traps:

  • Origin. PDF coordinates start bottom-left, in points (1/72 inch). Image/OCR coordinates start top-left, in pixels. Convert to one convention (e.g. PDF points, top-left origin, normalised 0–1) before storing.
  • Rotation and crop boxes. Rotated pages and cropped media boxes shift coordinates. Normalise using page size from the PDF.
def to_top_left_normalised(bbox_bottom_left, page_w, page_h):
    l, b, r, t = bbox_bottom_left            # PDF points, origin bottom-left
    return (l / page_w, (page_h - t) / page_h, r / page_w, (page_h - b) / page_h)

4. OCR and vision-language models

  • PaddleOCR — text detection + recognition, many languages (including Hindi and other Indic scripts), table recognition; PaddleOCR-VL adds a compact vision-language model for document parsing.
  • Vision-language models (VLMs) such as Qwen-VL, InternVL and Gemma 3 read a page image and answer questions or emit JSON. Strong on messy layouts, charts and handwritten notes; slower, need a GPU, and can hallucinate values.

A sensible pattern: OCR/layout tools for bulk extraction with coordinates; VLM as a second opinion on low-confidence or high-value fields, constrained to return JSON against a Pydantic schema; disagreements go to review.

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class IncomeStatementFields(BaseModel):
    revenue_from_operations: float | None = Field(description="In the unit stated in the table header")
    profit_after_tax: float | None
    unit: str                                   # 'INR crore', 'INR lakh', …
    fiscal_year: str
    page_number: int

# send IncomeStatementFields.model_json_schema() as the required output schema to the VLM,
# then IncomeStatementFields.model_validate_json(response_text)

5. Zero-shot entity extraction with GLiNER

GLiNER is a compact named-entity model that takes the labels as input, so you can extract new entity types without retraining.

from gliner import GLiNER

model = GLiNER.from_pretrained("urchade/gliner_medium-v2.1")   # pick a current checkpoint
text = ("The statutory auditor, ABC & Co LLP, resigned on 12 March 2026. "
        "Promoters have pledged 38% of their holding. The company breached the "
        "debt service coverage covenant under its term loan.")
labels = ["auditor name", "date", "pledge percentage", "covenant breach", "rating symbol"]

for ent in model.predict_entities(text, labels, threshold=0.45):
    print(ent["label"], "→", ent["text"], round(ent["score"], 2), ent["start"], ent["end"])

The start/end character offsets map back to the document's text spans, and through them to bounding boxes — so even entities keep provenance.

6. Financial sentiment and distress classification with FinBERT

FinBERT is BERT further trained on financial text, with a head classifying positive / negative / neutral.

from transformers import pipeline

clf = pipeline("text-classification", model="ProsusAI/finbert", top_k=None)
clf("Material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the company's ability to continue as a going concern.")
# [[{'label': 'negative', 'score': 0.9…}, {'label': 'neutral', …}, {'label': 'positive', …}]]

Distress signals worth classifying in filings:

Signal Where it appears
Going-concern doubt Auditor's report, notes
Qualified / adverse opinion, emphasis of matter Auditor's report
Auditor resignation Stock exchange disclosures
Covenant breach, default, restructuring Notes to accounts, rating rationales
Rating downgrade, "watch with negative implications" Rating rationales
Rising pledged promoter shares Shareholding disclosures

Generic sentiment is a weak signal on its own. Fine-tune a classifier on your own labelled paragraphs for these specific categories, and keep the model version with every prediction.

7. The evidence record

Every extracted value becomes an evidence row before it becomes a fact:

CREATE TABLE bronze.extracted_value (
  evidence_id       STRING,
  file_sha256       STRING,      -- the landed file
  page_number       INT,
  bbox              ARRAY<DOUBLE>,  -- [x0, y0, x1, y1], normalised, top-left origin
  raw_text          STRING,      -- exactly as read, e.g. '1,23,456.70'
  parsed_value      DECIMAL(24,4),
  unit              STRING,      -- after normalising '₹ in crore'
  field_name        STRING,      -- 'revenue_from_operations'
  fiscal_period     STRING,
  extractor         STRING,      -- 'docling 2.x / tableformer', 'paddleocr', 'vlm:qwen…'
  extractor_version STRING,
  confidence        DOUBLE,
  extracted_at      TIMESTAMP
);

Two practical normalisation rules for Indian documents:

  • Number format: 1,23,456.70 uses lakh grouping; strip commas before parsing. Brackets (1,234) mean negative.
  • Units: headers say ₹ in crore, ₹ in lakh, ₹ in million. 1 crore = 100 lakh = 10 million. Store a canonical unit.

8. Human review — the validation workbench

The reviewer sees the PDF page with the bounding box highlighted next to the extracted value, and can accept, correct or reject. Corrections are stored as labelled data:

  • feeds evaluation (precision/recall per field and extractor),
  • feeds fine-tuning of extractors,
  • creates a CORRECTION version in the bitemporal table (chapter 09) with the reviewer as approver.

Track extractor quality over time with a golden set of hand-verified documents; run it on every model or parser upgrade before rollout.

9. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why must every extracted number keep page and bounding box?
  2. A PDF bounding box (72, 700, 200, 720) on a 595×842 page — convert it to normalised top-left coordinates.
  3. When would you use a VLM rather than OCR + table parsing, and how do you guard against hallucinated numbers?
  4. Write the GLiNER labels you would use to detect promoter pledging and auditor changes.
  5. Parse (1,23,456.70) under the header ₹ in lakh into a canonical INR value.

10. Review checklist

  • Each page classified as digital or scanned; OCR only where needed.
  • Every extracted value stored with file hash, page, bbox, extractor version and confidence.
  • Coordinates normalised to one convention.
  • Indian number grouping, negatives in brackets and units normalised.
  • Low-confidence and high-value fields go to human review.
  • A golden set gates every extractor upgrade.
